# Products for children

## Scope

Applies when the change touches users under 13, minors in the EU or UK, or users of an app that a state age law covers. Not when the service is not directed to children and knowingly collects no child's data. Neighbours: `aidd-team:privacy-by-default`, `aidd-team:accessible-ui`, `aidd-team:technical-writing`, `aidd-team:education`, `aidd-team:games-and-interactive-media`.

## Terms

- **Child**: Under 13 for COPPA; under the digital-consent age in the EU, 13 to 16 by member state; under 18 for the UK Children's Code and the DSA.
- **Verifiable parental consent**: Consent by a method reasonably calculated to make sure it is the parent who gives it.
- **Actual knowledge**: Knowing a user is a child, which brings COPPA's duties to a general-audience service.
- **Age assurance**: Age estimation or verification, in proportion to the risk.
- **High privacy by default**: A child's settings start at their most private.

## Dated obligations

| From | Obligation | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2025-07-14 | The Commission's guidelines on the protection of minors are its yardstick for DSA Article 28(1) on every online platform accessible to minors. | S5 |
| 2025-07-24 | A UK service likely to be accessed by children has completed its children's risk assessment and protects children from harmful content. | S4 |
| 2025-12-10 | Australia: an age-restricted social media platform takes reasonable steps to keep Australian children under 16 from holding an account. | S8 |
| 2026-03-17 | Brazil's ECA Digital is in force for every digital product or service children and adolescents are likely to use. | S7 |
| 2026-04-22 | The amended COPPA Rule applies, except §312.11(d)(1), (d)(4), and (g) (safe-harbor duties, on their own dates). It requires separate parental consent for third-party disclosure, a written data retention policy, and a written information security program. | S1 |

## Invariants and missed cases

| Always true | The case a plan misses |
| --- | --- |
| No personal data from a child before consent, unless an exception applies. | An analytics or crash SDK that sends a device id at first launch. |
| A child's new feature starts at its most private setting. | A feature shipped with sharing or location on. |
| A child's data is kept only as long as its purpose needs, by a written policy. | Backups, logs, and the vendor's copy. |

## Checklist by loop step

| Step | Item | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Before the first edit (`aidd gate --paths`) | Users under 13, minors in the EU, or a UK service likely to be accessed by children: the privacy and compliance dimensions, major, the privacy pool. | S1, S3, S4 |
| Specify | Age assurance, verifiable parental consent, data minimization, and defaults (private by default, no profiling, no nudges) in the Acceptance. | S1, S2 |
| Specify | The age assurance method is chosen by risk (verification, estimation, or inference, stepped up where the harm is high), with its error rates. A neutral age screen sets no default age and gives no hint of the cut-off. Its fallback is never a dead end. Where a US state or national law requires it, the app reads the store's or the operating system's age signal, and the team checks each law's date at source. | S6, S4, S5 |
| Specify | A service that minors in Brazil use has age verification and parental supervision tools, and no ad profiling (ECA Digital). An Australian social media platform keeps under-16s from holding an account. | S7, S8 |
| Implement | No behavioral advertising, no geolocation by default, no dark pattern; plain-language notices; separate verifiable parental consent before any disclosure to third parties, targeted advertising included. A parent can review and delete their child's data and withdraw consent. | S2, S1, S5 |
| Review | Every flow of a child's data has a lawful basis and a retention limit that the published data retention policy states. The information security program covers the change. | S3, S1 |
| Roll out | Consent flows and data-subject requests are the observe signals; a broken consent flow rolls back. | S1 |

## Test commands

| Command | Proves | How | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Consent-flow tests | nothing is collected before consent, and nothing is disclosed to a third party without its separate consent | the team's `e2e-test` runner records every outbound request from first launch with no consent, and fails on a host outside the allow-list or a disclosure without its separate consent | S1 |
| Default-settings tests | private by default, no profiling, no geolocation | unit tests over each setting's default, and an end-to-end check of a new child account | S2 |
| Age-assurance tests | an under-age or unassured user reaches no restricted feature or content, and every assurance outcome has a path forward | end-to-end tests per age band and per assurance result (pass, fail, unsure) | S6, S4 |
| Inventory schema check | every flow of a child's data carries a lawful basis and a retention limit | a schema check over the data-flow inventory | S3 |
| SDK allow-list check | no ad or tracking SDK on the child surface | the SDK inventory diffed against a committed allow-list in CI, failing on any ad or tracking SDK | S1 |
| Parent rights test | a parent can review and delete their child's data and withdraw consent, and each takes effect | the team's `e2e-test` runner signs in as the parent, runs each action, and asserts its result through the API | S1 |

- From `aidd-team:technical-writing`: Reading-level check.

## Keep it current

Each entry is due after its `review_every_days` (else emerging 90 days, established 365) or by its `review_due`. An emerging one applies only when the change needs it, said in the Spec. One `aidd eval standards` lists as due is looked up in Specify, and a missing one is proposed to aidd's `schemas/industry-standards.json`.
